description: REST API and MCP server that validates IBANs and identifies the bank behind them: the BIC with its source, the bank-code check against the national register where one is read, SEPA reachability and the EPC Verification of Payee register listing. Also BIC/SWIFT and Swiss clearing lookups.
rules: Keyless trial: POST https://api.ibanforge.com/v1/iban/validate with {"iban": "..."} serves 25 validations a week per source address (reset Monday 00:00 UTC), on that route only. Use it to develop, not in production.
In production, send an API key in the header Authorization: Bearer ifk_... (X-API-Key also works). Keep the key on the server: never put it in browser code.

A free key needs no e-mail and no card: POST https://api.ibanforge.com/v1/keys/generate. Claimed with a 6-digit code mailed to an address the user chooses, it reaches 200 requests a month: https://ibanforge.com/docs/api-keys?src=context7
Validate up to 100 IBANs in one call with POST /v1/iban/batch and {"ibans": [...]}. The keyless trial does not cover it: send a key or pay with x402. Each IBAN uses one request or credit.
An invalid IBAN is not an HTTP error: the answer is 200 with valid: false, an error code (checksum_failed, wrong_length, ...) and error_detail.

Check the HTTP status before reading valid. A 402 has no valid field: no allowance left or payment needed, cause.reason says which (trial_exhausted, monthly_quota_exhausted). A 429 means over 100 requests a minute from one IP: wait for Retry-After.
Read the bank in bic.bank_name and bic.code, SEPA reachability in sepa.schemes, and whether the EPC VoP register lists the bank as ready in sepa.vop_participant.
IBANforge never checks the account holder's name and does not prove an account exists or is open: that is Verification of Payee, run by the payee's bank.
